newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi-Japan firm plans $139 mln recycling plants.
newsitem.headline: Saudi-Japan firm plans $139 mln recycling plants.

text.p: A Saudi-Japanese joint venture is planning to build two recycling plants in Riyadh and Jeddah at a cost of 520 million riyals ($139 million), the Saudi Gazette newspaper reported on Wednesday.

Sadaca Environmental Group -- a 75/25 joint venture between Saudi firm SKAB Commerce and Industry and Japan's Asahi Juken -- plans to start operating the Jeddah plant in early 1998 and the Riyadh plant a year later, the newspaper said.
The 220 million riyal Jeddah plant will be able to process 250,000 tonnes of garbage annually, while the 300 million riyal Riyadh plant will be capable of processing 500,000 tonnes.

"The recycling plants...(are) expected to generate electricity, create valuable compost and to recycle aluminium, glass, paper, plastic and other metals retrieved from garbage," the newspaper said. ($1=3.75 riyals)
